title: Skill Portfolios and Blended Career Paths — Playbook
author: Priya Desai
content:
Purpose and scope

This playbook documents Redwood's Skill Portfolio and Blended Career Paths framework. It explains how individuals and managers build transparent portfolios that combine competencies, project evidence, and stretch goals; how blended (matrixed) career paths work; and the operational steps for onboarding, calibration, and role transitions. Audience: all contributors, managers, and people-ops partners.

Why we adopted skill portfolios

- Move beyond title-only ladders: capture what people can do, not only where they sit in org charts.
- Support hybrid career moves: technical contributors can blend product, platform, or people-lead responsibilities without artificial transfers.
- Increase mobility, equity, and clarity: make expectations explicit so promotion and role change decisions are reproducible.

Key concepts

1) Skill portfolio (SP): a living document for an individual that lists 6–12 core skills, evidence items (projects, PR links, evals), current level per skill, and 3–6 near-term growth objectives. SPs are stored in the career-portfolio workspace and updated quarterly.

2) Blended career path (BCP): a named mix of competency emphases (for example: 60% Platform Engineering + 40% Product Strategy). Each BCP defines expected proficiency per competency, sample evidence, and suggested time-in-role for transitions.

3) Competency bands: We use a 5-band scale (Contributing, Experienced, Senior, Principal, Distinguished). Bands are defined per competency with observable behaviors.

Roles, owners, and time horizons

- Individual contributor: owns their SP, updates quarterly, books a 1:1 review with manager at least every 3 months.
- Manager: validates SP evidence, sets blended expectations, and owns development checkpoints. Responsible for running calibration panels for promotion proposals.
- People-ops: maintains templates, runs training on portfolio writing, and coordinates calibration sessions.

Eligibility rules and common scenarios

- Internal lateral move (same band, different focus): no formal promotion packet required. SP update + cross-team intro + new manager welcome checklist.
- Blended move (change of % emphasis but same band): SP + manager alignment note. HR records allocation (% split) and updates role profile.
- Promotion (band up): formal promotion packet required (portfolio snapshot, 3–5 evidence items, manager assessment, calibration panel). Typical minimum time-in-band: 12 months, exceptions require documented exceptional impact.

Manager checklist for new blended hires or transitions

1. Within 7 days: Meet with individual to align blended allocation and priorities.
2. Within 14 days: Agree on 3–6 quarter objectives and the SP template entries.
3. Within 30 days: Submit any role-allocation updates to HR via PeopleFlow (see tooling).
4. Quarterly: Run a development review; confirm evidence and next objectives.

Quarterly calibration and promotion process (high-level)

1. Manager prepares promotion packet (portfolio snapshot + manager writeup + reviewer nominations).
2. People-ops schedules calibration panel (composed of cross-functional seniors and an independent chair).
3. Panel scores against competency rubrics and returns a decision: approve, request more evidence, or deny.
4. If approved, HR prepares compensation and title update; rollout is coordinated with manager and communications template.

Templates, tooling, and examples

- Career Portfolio template: link to career-portfolio workspace (internal). Template fields: skill name, band level, evidence links, impact summary (100–250 words), 90-day goals, manager notes.
- PeopleFlow HRIS commands (example):
  - Submit allocation change: /peopleflow allocate --user @username --role "Platform/Product" --pct 40
  - Request promotion packet intake: /peopleflow promo-request --user @username --band candidate --mgr @mgr
- Slack shortcuts: use the "Career > Portfolio" slash menu in #people-ops to open templates.

Example portfolio table (as plain text)

| Skill | Band | Evidence (links) | 90-day priorities | Owner | Notes |
| Technical Design | Senior | github.com/rw/projA#PR234 | Reduce infra latency by 15% | @alex | Leads design reviews |
| Cross-team Influence | Experienced | doc/rw/oncall-collab | Run fortnightly sync with product | @alex | Focus on stakeholder comms |

Operational parameters and guardrails

- Minimum portfolio refresh cadence: quarterly.
- Time-in-band guidance: Contributing (6–18m), Experienced (12–24m), Senior (18–36m), Principal (24–48m), Distinguished (36m+). These are guidelines, not hard rules.
- Promotions require cross-functional evidence and at least one external peer reviewer.

Accessibility, fairness, and calibration controls

- Blind review option: for promotion panels, submit anonymized evidence where feasible.
- Calibration matrices include demographic signals (aggregate, not per-person) to detect unintended bias. People-ops will run disparity reports quarterly.

Metrics and signals we track

- Portfolio coverage: % of employees with a portfolio updated in the last 120 days (target: 90%).
- Internal mobility rate: % of role changes that happen via SP/BCP within 12 months (target: 18% annually).
- Promotion approval variance: panel approval rates by manager cohort (investigate >15% delta).

Rollout and training plan

1. Pilot (Q1 2026): 3 teams across Eng, Product, and SRE adopt SP + BCP. People-ops runs 2 workshops per team.
2. Feedback phase (Q2 2026): Collect experience surveys, refine templates, add automation to PeopleFlow.
3. Full rollout (Q3–Q4 2026): Company-wide training, manager certification, and inclusion in new-hire orientation.

Frequently asked questions (FAQ)

Q: Is an SP visible to my peers?
A: By default SPs are visible to your manager, people-ops, and anyone you explicitly share the link with. We encourage sharing parts of your SP with cross-functional partners for collaboration and mentorship.

Q: Can I be on two Blended Career Paths?
A: No — to keep expectations clear, each person has one primary BCP with explicit % allocation metadata recorded in PeopleFlow. Short-term project assignments can be noted as evidence and do not change BCP allocation.

Appendix: sample portfolio YAML (for automation)

```
name: Alex Johnson
role: Senior Software Engineer
bcp: Platform/Strategy
allocation: "60/40"
skills:
  - name: Technical Design
    band: Senior
    evidence:
      - type: github
        url: https://github.com/rw/projA/pull/234
  - name: Mentorship
    band: Experienced
    evidence: []
objectives:
  - title: Reduce inference tail latency by 15%
    due: 2026-06-30
```

Appendix: sample manager email templates and communications

- New blended assignment (subject): "Welcome: role allocation and priorities"
- Promotion outcome (subject): "Promotion decision & next steps" — includes approved band, new expectations, and a 30/60/90 development plan.

Ownership and escalation

- People-ops: maintain templates, run reports, host training. Primary contact: people-ops@redwood.com.
- Managers: ensure portfolio hygiene for their direct reports.
- Escalations: if a manager and individual disagree on allocation or promotion readiness, escalate to People-ops partner; unresolved disagreements escalate to the alignment committee.

Feedback and improvements

We iterate on SPs and BCPs. Submit improvement suggestions to the Career Playbook issue tracker (internal JIRA: CP-PLAY). People-ops will run a biannual review and publish changelogs.
